messages:
Priya: Quick follow-up to the release-warden RFC — I sketched an alternate split: keep fast traffic-weight decisions in the router, but centralize rollback/fallback choices in a separate Warden service that consumes fused signals (latency p50/p95, error-rate, quality regression score).
Oliver: +1 on separating fast path from policy brain. question: how do we avoid split-brain when router and warden disagree?
Priya: Router keeps provisional weights; warden can issue authoritative commands via a single control channel. Router falls back to locally cached emergency policy if it loses contact with warden for >30s.
Jaime: What happens to A-B experiments? We need per-experiment guardrails not just global thresholds.
Priya: Plan: warden maintains experiment-scoped policies and a soft-stall for new cohorts. Router tags requests with experiment id and applies local transforms, but defers cutoff to warden.
Sarah: Telemetry: need clear contract for signal cadence. If warden only sees 1m aggregates we might miss fast regressions. Can we ship a hybrid: 5s rolling metrics for p50/p95, aggregated quality signals every 30s?
Oliver: Tradeoff: shorter cadence increases noise and cost. Suggest exponential smoothing on metrics at warden to reduce flapping.
Jaime: Also consider quality signals from offline evals — not just production. Warden can ingest eval verdicts via the same pipeline and weight them.
Priya: Good note. Another tradeoff: should warden be allowed to execute rollbacks automatically, or just recommend and require human approval above some severity?
Sarah: For low-severity regressions (small latency or minor error bump) auto-fallback is fine. For model-quality regressions we should require an opt-in flag per experiment to enable auto-rollback.
Priya: Agreed. Proposed policy tiers: auto, supervised-auto (notif + auto on big delta), manual. Default supervised-auto for new experiments.
deploy-bot: :rocket: staging/edge canary deployed to 5% for experiment=nlp-draft (sha: f3a1c2).
Oliver: Edge case: partial degradations where latency spikes for a subset of tenants. Warden needs per-tenant slice awareness and tenant-scoped rollbacks.
Priya: We'll include tenant dimension in the signal schema. Router should support per-tenant overrides and isolation. Plan B: if tenant isolation not available, fallback to global rollback.
Jaime: Interface boundary: expose a small RPC for "apply-policy" with fields {policy_id, scope, ttl, reason, operator} and a read-only stream for "policy-events". Keep it simple.
Priya: Exactly. Also a health handshake: router registers shards with warden and reports last-uptime/lag. If router sees >2 consecutive missed heartbeats from warden, it scales back to safe mode.
Sarah: Monitoring: add a canary-health dashboard with a per-experiment scorecard: latency trends, quality regression rate, rollback history. Also a Slack webhook for critical triggers.
Priya: Ops flow: warden decides -> posts decision (auto/apply) -> router acknowledges -> deploy-bot notes rollout/rollback. All decisions logged for audit and postmortem.
Jaime: One more: what about staged rollbacks (50% -> 0%) vs instant cut? Staged is safer but slower to reduce impact.
Priya: Make staged configurable per-policy. Default: staged(5%, 1m, 0) for model switches. Instant for infra failures.
Oliver: Implementation notes: prefer event-sourced decisions so we can replay and reason. Keep control plane lightweight, move heavy aggregation to a telemetry worker cluster.
Sarah: Sounds good. I'll prototype a small metrics smoothing lib for warden and share API stubs.
Priya: Thanks — can everyone drop any hard objections here by EOD? I'll collate and update the RFC with the warden control-channel sketch and policy tiers.
Jaime: No objections from me. Thanks.
Oliver: LGTM.
deploy-bot: :information_source: note: policy apply events will be logged at /infra/warden/events and surfaced in the console.
